verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit documents its own noise-reduction controls. It learns review preferences from chat feedback, path filters exclude lock files and generated code, incremental review covers only new changes, and Change Stack findings help decide what to fix first. However, no evidence documents explicit severity labels, comment deduplication, or false-positive rates, and community reports are mixed: one team removed it as "too verbose" with "too many false positives", while others praise "clean, actionable PR reviews." Missing for 10: documented severity labels on comments, explicit comment deduplication, measured or independently confirmed low false-positive rates.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, the reviewer keeps noise low — few false positives, deduplicated comments, severity labels — so my team doesn't tune it out

citations.quote: Review preferences CodeRabbit learns from your chat conversations and applies automatically to future reviews.
Path filters exclude files that don't benefit from review: lock files, binaries, and generated code.
@coderabbitai review does incremental review (new changes), not a full review.
Read what CodeRabbit found in a change, judge how ready it is to merge, and decide what to fix first.
Love the product clean, actionable PR reviews.
